verdict.rationale: mise documents keeping incumbent asdf conventions: it reads `.tool-versions` as-is, honors idiomatic files like `.node-version`/`.ruby-version`, can still use asdf plugins, and offers a shims mode. Community users describe it as a "drop-in asdf replacement" with the same functionality, but the evidence never shows familiar incumbent command names (e.g. asdf-style subcommands or aliases) working unchanged; users must learn `mise use`, `mise install` and `mise exec`. Missing for 10: documented command-level compatibility or aliases for asdf/nvm/pyenv commands, and a first-party migration guide mapping incumbent commands to mise equivalents.
